content: The core of a coronary guidewire plays a critical role in determining the device's performance characteristics. Typically, the core is tapered towards the distal end, where the tip is attached. If the tapering begins closer to the tip, the guidewire becomes more rigid, offering enhanced steerability and torque control. Conversely, if the tapering starts more proximally, the guidewire has a longer, more flexible tip. The core can either be continuous or joined. Joined cores are more prone to bending or prolapsing during advancement. Guidewire cores made of stainless steel are stiffer, providing superior support and torque control. On the other hand, nitinol cores are significantly more flexible. Composition of Guidewire Cores The core of a guidewire is typically made from nitinol, stainless steel, or a similar metal. Nitinol Guidewire Cores Nitinol is a super-elastic alloy that offers several advantages: It is designed to resist kinking. It provides excellent flexibility and steering capabilities. It is likely to be more durable. It offers better trackability. It reduces the risk of prolapse. However, nitinol cores have some disadvantages: They may be less torquable compared to other materials. They can store torque without effectively transmitting it to the tip. Single nitinol cores may wind up, storing torque instead of releasing it efficiently. Clinical Applications of Nitinol Cores Due to their flexibility and durability, nitinol guidewires are particularly useful in navigating retroflexed coronary arteries, such as the circumflex artery. Stainless Steel Guidewire Cores Stainless steel was the original material used for coronary guidewire cores. It offers several advantages: It provides excellent pushability, support, and torque control. It allows for good shape retention in core-to-tip designs. However, stainless steel cores have some limitations: They are more prone to kinking. They are less flexible compared to newer materials like nitinol. High Tensile Strength Stainless Steel High tensile strength stainless steel is an advanced form of the traditional stainless steel core. It offers the following benefits: Greater durability compared to standard stainless steel. Better shape retention. Improved flexibility. Enhanced steering and tracking capabilities. Asahi Tru Torque Steel The Asahi Tru Torque Steel guidewire core is another specialized design, offering unique performance characteristics.
